The last case is the hardest of the four in its data. The original author (OA) asked whether the economic crisis changed how citizens of the European Union frame the Union, and answered from sixteen waves of the Eurobarometer, ten years of surveys in twenty-seven member states. The claim is about countries in years, while the surveys hold respondents, so the analysis rests on a panel of country-years built by averaging the answers of each country in each year, and on models for such a panel: fixed effects, random effects and the within–between model. This week you download the sixteen files, turn them into the panel with the scripts of the workspace, and reproduce the value that Multi100 recorded for analyst C6HJR. The files come under the terms of use of GESIS, which forbid passing them on: they stay on your own machine, out of every repository and out of any session that an AI assistant can read.

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| The paper of the OA [@Teney2016DoesEUEconomic] | Before class. Read the whole article: the two hypotheses about economic crisis and the framing of the EU, the question on what the EU means to the respondent, the macro indicators, the multilevel models, and the sentence from which SCORE took the claim. | 60 minutes |
| [Case study](../../cases/eu-frames/index.qmd), sections 1 and 3 | Before class. [The original study](../../cases/eu-frames/index.qmd#sec-study), its data, the selections made by the OA and the focal estimate; then [the five reanalysts](../../cases/eu-frames/index.qmd#sec-reanalysts), each in turn, with an assessment of their choices and the coding errors that two of them made. | 40 minutes |
| [Setup](../../setup.qmd#the-workspace) | Before class, Task 1 of the case. Download the workspace of the EU-frames case and run `source("R/check_setup.R")` until every line prints OK. | 15 minutes |
| [Social science data sources](../../companion/data-sources.qmd#sec-gesis), section 3.1 | Download the sixteen Eurobarometer files from GESIS with the account that you opened in week 9, following the steps screen by screen, and read what the terms of use allow and what they forbid. | 45 minutes |
| [Building the analysis file](../../companion/data-management.qmd) | Run the first script of the workspace on your sixteen files and read the report that it prints; then work through the second, which scores the items into scales, deals with the respondents who named nothing, averages the respondents into country-years with and without survey weights, merges the macro series, and reproduces the panel of the course. | 45 minutes |
| [The statistical methods behind the course](../../companion/stats-methods.qmd#sec-aggregation), section 1 | Why the predictor is measured at the country-year, and what a cell mean is a mean of. | 20 minutes |
| Slides, Part 2, and Task 2 in your report or working script, or [Browser lab](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd#task-2-get-the-data-and-look-at-it) Task 2 | In class. The paper, the claim and the five analysts; meet the panel of 270 country-years and draw the outcome country by country; write the [estimand statement](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd#task-4-estimand-and-dag) and finish the graph, and write two sentences on what two-way fixed effects adjust for and what they cannot fix. The estimands run and the causal-graph crash course repeat week 3, so the class passes over them. | 45 minutes |
| Slides, [Part 3](../../slides/eu-frames-full.html#/part-3-reproduction-and-exploration), and Task 3 in your report or [Browser lab](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd#task-3-reproduce-the-recorded-result) | In class. The instruction of Task 2 of Multi100, then the reproduction: the two-way fixed-effects model of the cosmopolitan share on the centred unemployment rate, fitted with `fixest::feols()` and conventional standard errors. It gives *t* = −3.804 on 233 degrees of freedom, the value that Multi100 recorded for C6HJR. | 30 minutes |
| [The statistical methods behind the course](../../companion/stats-methods.qmd#sec-fe), sections 4 and 5 | Country fixed effects and two-way fixed effects, and what each comparison holds constant; then within and between, random effects and the Hausman test, and the within–between model that gives each kind of variation its own slope. | 50 minutes |

**By the end of the session** you have the sixteen files on your machine and the panel of the course rebuilt from them by the scripts of the workspace, *t* = −3.804 reproduced yourself, the estimand behind the claim written in one sentence, and two sentences on what two-way fixed effects absorb and what they leave.
